clue.text: Drink port and heave

parts.note: Singapore is a major Asian seaport
to heave something is to throw or fling it

explanation.surface: Someone drinks port and then is sick, a familiar sequence after a heavy night.
explanation.definitionFit: The Singapore Sling is a gin-based cocktail first mixed at Raffles Hotel, so it is a mixed alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Dope out of seasoning for cake layer?

indicators.note: taking something out of a word means removing those letters from it

parts.note: spicing a dish is seasoning it
SP, short for starting price, is slang for the inside information or lowdown

explanation.surface: A cook seems to be advised to leave drugs out of the seasoning used for a cake.
explanation.walkthrough: Dope here is information, not a drug: SP is the racing term for the lowdown, as in 'what's the SP?'. Removing it from SPICING leaves ICING.
explanation.definitionFit: Icing is the sugary coating spread over a cake, so it forms the top layer; the question mark flags that it is one example.

clue.text: Gazette, in margins, to advertise produce

indicators.note: the margins of a word are its two edges, so only its first and last letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of Gazette
to tout goods is to advertise or solicit custom for them

explanation.surface: A newspaper seems to run small ads in its margins to promote farm produce.
explanation.definitionFit: To get out a product is to produce or issue it, as in getting out a new edition.

clue.text: Explorer's fruit and meat sustaining squad ultimately

parts.note: a pear is a fruit

indicators.note: sustaining means holding up from inside, so one piece is held within the other

parts.note: liver is offal eaten as meat

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word just before it

parts.note: the last letter of squad

explanation.surface: An explorer's supplies of fruit and meat keep a team going on an expedition.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay. D goes inside LIVER after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A pearl diver explores the seabed searching for oysters, so is a kind of underwater explorer.

clue.text: Crested waves, with German river eddying?

definitions.note: rode means crested when said of waves, as in a surfer rode the waves

indicators.note: eddying water circles round, so the letters go round with the last one moving to the front

parts.note: the Oder runs along the German–Polish border

explanation.surface: A boat seems to ride the waves of a swirling German river.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking the final R of ODER round to the front gives RODE.
explanation.definitionFit: To crest waves is to ride over their tops, so the past tense rode fits crested waves.

clue.text: Increasingly dingy? Forecaster maintains "go west"

indicators.note: to maintain is to hold or keep, so one word is kept inside the other

parts.note: a seer foretells the future
to go west is an idiom for dying

explanation.surface: A weather forecaster insists that conditions will move westwards and get gloomier.
explanation.walkthrough: To go west means to die, from the setting sun.
explanation.definitionFit: Seedier is the comparative of seedy, shabby and squalid, so it means more dingy.

clue.text: Private transport that's subject to inflation

parts.note: private thoughts are inner ones
the Tube is the London Underground

explanation.surface: Owning private transport seems to suffer from the rising cost of living.
explanation.walkthrough: Inflation looks economic, but it is pumping air into something.
explanation.definitionFit: An inner tube is the rubber ring inside a tyre that gets pumped up with air.

clue.text: Declining movement of Etonians before game?

definitions.meaning: second meaning, read literally: boys heading off to play the Eton wall game

explanation.walkthrough: Eton College has its own Wall Game, played against a brick wall, so pupils off to play it are literally heading to the wall.
explanation.definitionFit: Going to the wall is an idiom for failing or going bankrupt, so it means declining to ruin.

clue.text: Actress that is honourable kept within rules

indicators.note: kept within means held inside, so two pieces go between the others

parts.note: two rules: a bill, a proposed law, and a law
i.e. abbreviates id est, meaning that is
white is an old word for honourable or decent, as in 'that's very white of you'

explanation.surface: An actress who behaves honourably keeps within the rules.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural 'rules' is the key: it supplies two separate words for a rule, a proposed one and an enacted one, with the rest placed between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Billie Whitelaw was a British actress, best known for her work with Samuel Beckett.

clue.text: Prompt Jack perhaps to back turkey

parts.note: a turkey is slang for a fool
a jack is an example of a playing card

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to support a man named Jack in some contest against a turkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to back' places the card behind the turkey, so the turkey comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiot card is a cue board held up out of shot to remind a television presenter of the lines.

clue.text: Spartan character in denim stripped boring property

indicators.note: in places the first piece inside the second
stripped means peeled bare, so the outside letters are taken off

parts.note: nu is a letter of the Greek alphabet, as used in Sparta
taken as written

explanation.surface: A spartan figure in faded denim seems to describe a dull piece of real estate.
explanation.walkthrough: Spartan suggests austere, but here it means Greek, so the character is a letter of the Greek alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is listless boredom, the quality something tedious has, so it is the property of being boring.

clue.text: Josh's illustrating page during calm interval

indicators.note: during means within a stretch of time, so these pieces sit inside the other

parts.note: a lull is a quiet pause
e.g., for example, introduces an illustration
p is the abbreviation for page

explanation.surface: Someone named Josh is drawing a page of a picture book during a quiet break.
explanation.walkthrough: Josh looks like a name but is the verb or noun for teasing; the 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A josh is a good-natured tease, which is just what a leg-pull is: a playful joke at someone's expense.

clue.text: Roughnecks here identified by greaser gear

parts.note: oil is what greases machinery
rig means equipment or outfit

explanation.surface: Tough types are recognised by their greasy clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Roughnecks look like thugs, but it is the name for drilling crew.
explanation.definitionFit: A roughneck is a labourer on a drilling crew, so an offshore platform is where roughnecks work.

clue.text: Numerical data still entertains first son

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to have them in, so one piece is held inside

parts.note: static means motionless
1st, written IST, is first
s is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Numbers seem to show a family still hosting their firstborn.
explanation.definitionFit: Statistics are collected figures, so the word is a synonym for numerical facts.

clue.text: Dash from final exam to reflect

indicators.note: a reflection is a mirror image, so the letters are read backwards
from says the letters are taken out of the words that follow

parts.note: letters running across fiNAL Exam

explanation.surface: A student rushes out of a final exam to think it over.
explanation.definitionFit: Elan is flair and vigour, the same quality as dash, meaning style and spirit.

clue.text: Touring stately territory, go to Pierre's particular ground

indicators.note: touring means going around, so one word surrounds the other

parts.note: aller is French for to go, as a Frenchman like Pierre would say
a country seat is an estate with a stately home

explanation.surface: A Frenchman tours stately homes before visiting his favourite stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: Pierre stands for any Frenchman.
explanation.definitionFit: An all-seater is a stadium with seats for every spectator and no standing terraces, so a specific kind of sports ground.

clue.text: Writer who wins over press, after exchange

indicators.note: after an exchange the two pieces swap places, so the first goes to the back

parts.note: a victor is one who wins
o is the cricket scorebook abbreviation for over
to press someone close is to hug them

explanation.surface: A writer who wins awards seems to win over the press after a heated exchange.
explanation.definitionFit: Victor Hugo was the French novelist who wrote Les Misérables, so he is a writer.

clue.text: Boy down there finally rides Chopper more than once

parts.note: hell is traditionally the place below

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the next word

parts.note: the last letter of rides
a chopper is a tooth, and more than one makes them plural

explanation.surface: A lad from the underworld rides a Chopper bicycle again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: A Chopper was a popular 1970s British children's bike with high handlebars; here a chopper is a tooth.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Boy!' is an exclamation of surprise or annoyance, just as 'hell's teeth!' is a mild oath.

clue.text: Postman's central Stockport batch of letters picked up somewhere squalid

parts.note: SK1 is the postcode district for central Stockport, and the 1 looks like an I

indicators.note: in a down clue picking something up lifts it, so the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: a word is a group of letters

explanation.surface: A postman picks up a sack of mail in central Stockport before heading somewhere grim.
explanation.walkthrough: Stockport is a town near Manchester whose postcodes begin SK.
explanation.definitionFit: Skid row is a run-down district where down-and-outs live, so a squalid place.

clue.text: For certain European, retrospective festival's engrossing

indicators.note: retrospective looks back, so the word is read from end to start
engrossing means absorbing, so one piece is taken inside another

parts.note: Hay is the literary festival at Hay-on-Wye in Wales
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A European arts festival is staging a retrospective that certainly holds the attention.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeah is informal yes, an assent meaning for sure or certainly.

clue.text: Alpha males probing that woman's athletics equipment

indicators.note: probing means pushing into something, so these letters go inside

parts.note: her is the possessive for that woman
Alpha is A in the NATO alphabet
m is the abbreviation for male, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Dominant men seem to be nosing into a woman's sports kit.
explanation.walkthrough: Alpha males reads as a stock phrase but splits into A plus two Ms.
explanation.definitionFit: The hammer is a heavy metal ball on a wire thrown in the field events of athletics.

clue.text: Mark visiting mentioned security in wardrobe?

indicators.note: mentioned means spoken of, so it is the sound of the word that counts

parts.note: to type is to mark or print letters
someone visiting is in, at home

explanation.surface: A visitor seems to leave a mark on security arrangements in a clothes cupboard.
explanation.walkthrough: The spelling TIEP is chosen to fit the answer, since TIE sounds like the start of type.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiepin holds a necktie securely in place, so it is a piece of security for an item of clothing.

clue.text: Scraps for bird

parts.note: first scrap: to spar is to fight
second scrap: a row is a quarrel

explanation.surface: Leftover food is put out for a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: Scraps looks like leftovers but means fights, and the plural gives two of them.
explanation.definitionFit: The sparrow is a small brown bird, so it is an example of a bird.

clue.text: Potential place for lush borders in Edinburgh tended by Scotsman

indicators.note: something tended is looked after and enclosed, so it sits inside the other

parts.note: Rab is a Scottish form of Robert

indicators.note: the borders of a word are its edges, so only the first and last letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of Edinburgh

explanation.surface: A Scottish gardener tends the lush borders in an Edinburgh park.
explanation.walkthrough: Lush looks like an adjective for plants but is a noun meaning drunkard.
explanation.definitionFit: Rehab is a clinic for treating addiction, so a place a heavy drinker might be sent.

clue.text: Excessive drop of Olbas Oil

parts.note: OTT is short for over the top

indicators.note: a drop is a tiny amount, so only the first letter is taken

parts.note: the first letter of Olbas

explanation.surface: Someone is using too much Olbas Oil, a British decongestant inhaled for colds.
explanation.definitionFit: Otto, also attar, is a fragrant essential oil distilled from rose petals.

clue.text: Fed cracks case of larcener, getting cheers in NYPD

indicators.note: cracking something opens it up, so the first piece goes inside
the case of a word is its outer shell, its first and last letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of larcener
fed means ate a meal

explanation.surface: An FBI agent solves a theft case and is applauded by New York police.
explanation.walkthrough: Fed looks like an FBI agent but is the past tense of feed. Cheers here is the British goodbye, not applause.
explanation.definitionFit: Later is American slang for goodbye, the way Britons say cheers when leaving, so it is cheers as a New York cop says it.

clue.text: Old car rally — working out the odds of victory

parts.note: Triumph was a British car maker that closed in the 1980s

indicators.note: working out means removing, so the odd-numbered letters go and the even ones stay

parts.note: the second and fourth letters of rally

explanation.surface: A classic car rally is working out the betting on who will win.
explanation.definitionFit: Triumphal means relating to or celebrating a victory, as in a triumphal arch.

clue.text: Steal timber axes, then serve time here?

parts.note: to steal along or worm is to move stealthily
timber is wood
to scrub a plan is to cancel or axe it

explanation.surface: A thief steals timber and axes and then ends up in prison.
explanation.walkthrough: Wormwood Scrubs is a prison in west London.
explanation.definitionFit: Wormwood Scrubs is a London jail where offenders are locked up, so a place to serve a sentence.
